name: GtoPdb_search_targets
description: Search the Guide to Pharmacology database (GtoPdb) for drug targets with recoverable local offset pagination over the complete upstream response. Returns target IDs, names, abbreviations, types, and family classifications. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true. No authentication required.

name.description: Target NAME substring to search. Examples: 'dopamine', 'serotonin receptor', 'beta-adrenoceptor', 'TRPV1'. This is a name/abbreviation match, not a gene lookup -- GtoPdb names targets pharmacologically ('5-HT6 receptor', 'GluN2B'), so HGNC symbols such as 'HTR6' or 'GRIN2B' return nothing here. Use 'gene_symbol' for HGNC symbols.

gene_symbol.description: HGNC gene symbol for an exact target lookup. Examples: 'CHRNA7' (nicotinic acetylcholine receptor alpha7 subunit), 'GRIN2B' (GluN2B), 'HTR6' (5-HT6 receptor). Preferred over 'name' when you have a gene symbol.

type.description: Target type filter. Values: 'GPCR', 'Ion channel', 'Nuclear receptor', 'Enzyme', 'Transporter', 'Catalytic receptor'

query.description: Name/keyword to search for. Alias for the "name" parameter.

limit.description: Number of targets on this page (1-1000; default 50).

offset.description: Zero-based target offset. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true.

name: GtoPdb_search_ligands
description: Search the Guide to Pharmacology database for pharmacological ligands with recoverable local offset pagination over the complete upstream response. Returns ligand details including type, approval status, INN name, and WHO essential-medicine status. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true. No authentication required.

name.description: Ligand name or INN to search. Examples: 'aspirin', 'morphine', 'dopamine', 'caffeine', 'insulin'

type.description: Ligand type filter. Values: 'Approved', 'Synthetic organic', 'Natural product', 'Endogenous peptide', 'Antibody', 'Inorganic'

approved.description: Filter to approved drugs only (true) or all ligands (false/omit)

query.description: Name/keyword to search for. Alias for the "name" parameter.

limit.description: Number of ligands on this page (1-1000; default 50).

offset.description: Zero-based ligand offset. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true.

name: GtoPdb_get_interactions
description: Get pharmacological interactions between targets and ligands from the Guide to Pharmacology database. Results are recoverably paginated: start with offset=0 and continue with next_offset while has_more is true. Provide gene_symbol (convenience, auto-resolves to targetId), targetId (from GtoPdb_search_targets), or ligandId (from GtoPdb_search_ligands) to filter interactions. Set approved_only=true to cross-reference the GtoPdb ligand registry and retain only interactions whose ligand is explicitly approved; if that secondary lookup fails, the tool returns an error rather than silently returning unfiltered records. Returns binding affinity (Ki, Kd, IC50, EC50), action type, species, and assay information. No authentication required.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol convenience parameter — automatically resolves to GtoPdb targetId. Works for gene-symbol-named targets (e.g., 'KRAS', 'EGFR', 'BRAF', 'ALK'). Traditional receptor names like 'DRD2' may not resolve; use GtoPdb_search_targets first to confirm. Prefer exact gene symbols over partial names.

targetId.description: GtoPdb target ID. Get from GtoPdb_search_targets. Examples: 2486 (dopamine beta-hydroxylase), 20 (5-HT1A receptor). Alias: target_id also accepted.

target_id.description: Alias for targetId. GtoPdb target ID.

ligandId.description: GtoPdb ligand ID. Get from GtoPdb_search_ligands. Examples: 5765 (aspirin), 7093 (morphine)

approved_only.description: If true, retain only interactions whose ligandId is marked approved in the GtoPdb ligand registry. This is an exact client-side cross-reference; failure of the registry lookup returns an error, never unfiltered success.

limit.description: Maximum interactions to return on this page.

offset.description: Zero-based interaction offset. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true.

name: GtoPdb_search_diseases
description: Search the Guide to Pharmacology (GtoPdb / IUPHAR-BPS) for diseases with recoverable local offset pagination over the complete upstream response. Returns curated disease IDs, names, synonyms, and external cross-references. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true. No authentication required.

name.description: Disease name to search. Examples: 'epilepsy', 'asthma', 'hypertension', 'breast cancer'.

query.description: Name/keyword to search for. Alias for the "name" parameter.

limit.description: Number of diseases on this page (1-1000; default 50).

offset.description: Zero-based disease offset. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true.

name: GtoPdb_get_ligand_properties
description: Get the chemical structure and computed molecular properties of a ligand from the Guide to Pharmacology (GtoPdb / IUPHAR-BPS) by its ligand ID. Merges two keyless endpoints into one record: structure (canonical SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, IUPAC name) and molecularProperties (molecular weight, logP, hydrogen-bond donors/acceptors, rotatable bonds, topological polar surface area, Lipinski rule-of-five violation count). Use GtoPdb_search_ligands first to find a ligand_id (e.g., aspirin = 4139). No authentication required.

ligand_id.description: GtoPdb ligand ID. Get from GtoPdb_search_ligands. Examples: 4139 (aspirin), 1 (a-bungarotoxin). Alias: ligandId also accepted.

ligandId.description: Alias for ligand_id. GtoPdb ligand ID.

name: GtoPdb_get_disease_associations
description: Get curated disease-to-target and disease-to-ligand associations from the Guide to Pharmacology (GtoPdb / IUPHAR-BPS) for a given disease ID. Merges two keyless endpoints into one record: diseaseTargets (drug targets linked to the disease, with roles, references, and ligand-target interactions) and diseaseLigands (approved/experimental ligands linked to the disease, with approval status and clinical-use notes). An empty list is a valid result (some diseases have targets but no curated ligands). Use GtoPdb_search_diseases first to find a disease_id (e.g., non-allergic asthma = 1161). No authentication required.

disease_id.description: GtoPdb disease ID. Get from GtoPdb_search_diseases. Examples: 1161 (non-allergic asthma), 34 (acute myeloid leukemia). Alias: diseaseId also accepted.

diseaseId.description: Alias for disease_id. GtoPdb disease ID.
